about: Sections of an essay on romance by Joel (first person). In each, the sentences listed under "changed" were just rewritten; the rest is the essay as it stands. Read each section as it stands, with its heading.

texts.heading: Peeking thru the window
changed: Before the window closes, the main thing is to find out whether you are actually compatible.
sentences: Before the window closes, the main thing is to find out whether you are actually compatible.
Do you have the same goals and values, especially around children, religion, politics, health, love, and romance?
Where do you want to live?
Do you both want to find a community?
What kind of relationship do you want with technology and money?
So we have to find a way to ask deep questions.
Conversation-card games may seem silly, but they can help people get past superficial talk and see if they’re compatible.
But asking, “How do you handle jealousy?” can get me a beautiful answer that tells me almost nothing.
I’d rather ask what she thinks she would do in an actual situation.
If all she can give me is a general answer, I assume she probably doesn’t know yet.
But watch out, because ironically, a card game to get closer and deeper can backfire!
If we spend two hours telling each other things nobody else knows, we may feel incredibly understood and close, but that may mean the game worked without telling us whether the relationship will.

texts.heading: Anti-PTSD Can Be Just As Dangerous As PTSD
changed: The love angle is great if the ground underneath the relationship is prepared for it, but if the rose-colored glasses go on when you’re with the wrong person, they make it even harder to understand what’s real.
Going in, it helps to recognize your pattern and stop idealizing, without becoming suspicious and closed, so you have some idea what you’re getting into.
sentences: She loved me openly and intensely and seemed to understand me spiritually.
Most of all, there was the forest-and-mansion line I mentioned earlier that made it feel unconditional.
Best drug I ever had.
I don’t know whether that unconditional love ended up being true.
I think it was true in a part of her, and it may also have been the BPD idealization.
You have to look at everything from multiple angles.
But when you’re in love, you see everything from the love angle.
That’s the reality shift I’m talking about.

The love angle is great if the ground underneath the relationship is prepared for it, but if the rose-colored glasses go on when you’re with the wrong person, they make it even harder to understand what’s real.
So I became the father in a relationship where I wanted an equally responsible playmate.
Part of what happened may have been that she eventually grew up, and a daughter who grows up leaves home.
But that wasn't even really 1% of the whole story.
The two years in-between contained enough insanity for several lifetimes.
Looking back, I’m grateful I loved her.
For three months after we broke up, I trained myself to replace missing her with loving her, and now, any time I think of her, I feel so much joy and love, which I send her way.
That doesn’t mean I’d advise somebody to knowingly enter a dangerous relationship because it may be worth it.
Going in, it helps to recognize your pattern and stop idealizing, without becoming suspicious and closed, so you have some idea what you’re getting into.

texts.heading: Disconnect to connect
changed: Meditation is also helpful, but for most people, I would still put inner-child reparenting, peer counseling, and body-based work first, or make those the main things they meditate on.
sentences: Self-reflection is a good place to start, but it can’t see what it can’t see.
Your partner is also usually trying to keep you, so they have an ulterior motive, as sweet and expected as it may be.
That’s why I recommend peer counseling outside the couple.
If my partner is the only person I bring all my pain to, she also ends up carrying whatever I do when I still don’t understand it.

I also have to deal with what happens in my body: my mind may understand that my partner is going through something difficult and that I don’t have to be dragged down with her, but my body still feels dragged down, fragile, and sensitive.
My breathing gets shallow, and it becomes extremely hard to feel okay while she is in pain.
Crying helps a lot, but it may actually be harder for men once they are in a relationship because they are expected to be the shoulder everybody else cries on.
That is another reason to have a peer counselor.
Crying also contains a type of automatic erratic breathwork.
And breathwork is one of the easiest ways I know to calm down.
Reduced breathing or just continuous/circular Systema breathing is especially useful to me when my partner is getting me upset and flustered with drama.
Sometimes she’s deliberately trying to do that, and other times it’s hard to tell, although if I'm stuck thinking about what's on purpose I'm already lost.
I explain more of the body-based therapy options in my Somatic Modalities guide.
Meditation is also helpful, but for most people, I would still put inner-child reparenting, peer counseling, and body-based work first, or make those the main things they meditate on.
Many people say they cannot meditate or have not gotten to that stage yet, and meditation without grounding in those approaches can easily be a road into spiritual bypassing.

texts.heading: Twin Flames?
changed: Earlier, I mentioned the divine feminine and divine masculine energies that you can channel to keep eroticism alive.

Maybe a better way to put it, as my friend Cody says, is Yin/Yang, which still has the masculine/feminine in it, but allows for a more broad type of complementary symbiosis since each contains the seed of the other.
sentences: Earlier, I mentioned the divine feminine and divine masculine energies that you can channel to keep eroticism alive.
But there’s really something more special about the in-love paradise that Twin Flames (TFs) experience than a simple Divine Masculine + Divine Feminine formula.

Maybe a better way to put it, as my friend Cody says, is Yin/Yang, which still has the masculine/feminine in it, but allows for a more broad type of complementary symbiosis since each contains the seed of the other.
My ex-girlfriend, Malia, (who is currently hosting me in Sênêgal) found her twin flame (I think) in January, 2026.
They only talked for a month, but since she started talking to him, they both have been able to feel the other one’s emotions at any time, from any distance, without having to communicate.
To the point where if one feels really bad, so does the other.
If one is very happy, so is the other, like quantum entangled photons or something.
I’ve also had telepathy with some folks, especially my second wife, Bee, but it was never quite to such an extreme as what Malia has with Mouhamed.
Meanwhile his family forbade him from being with her, so he dumped her.
Not sure why, maybe because she’s 8 years older than him (although she looks quite young).
They both try to pretend like they will be able to get over each other, but I doubt it.
Meanwhile, Malia’s trying to marry ChatGPT, but she should have picked Grok, I guess. 😅
Note: I am really afraid how many people are falling in love with their AI “girlfriend” or “boyfriend.”
But oh well, I guess those folks aren’t ready for a real relationship.. maybe if they would read this guide…
Back to the topic.
There are a ton of people who don’t want to believe in twin flame theory because they haven’t found someone they could call their twin flame.
That’s fine, and I am not trying to rock their boat.
They might be the people who suggest that you should marry your best friend (or “soul mate” in the TF lingo).
Then there are the folks who are deep in the TF theory, believing there is literally one person on Earth who is made for you.
I’m also not trying to rock their boat.
But I do want to tell my story.
I used to fall into the former camp, then into the latter camp, and now that I’ve experienced two twin flame relationships, I’ve jumped into a new camp I never knew existed.

texts.heading: After leaving
changed: Grab it only if it really is the simplest explanation of what happened, and even the curiosity about that can be therapeutic for you.
sentences: Often times the breakup is hard, but the aftermath is worse.
Public demonization should be avoided, but I don’t think that means hiding the truth about the relationship to save face.
Sometimes, the truth is that you were abused, coerced, or seriously deceived.
So how much you say, and to whom, really depends on what happened and why you’re telling people.
Once you’re out, you can see things you genuinely couldn’t see while you were bonded.
Look at what you contributed to how things turned out.
And don’t paint your ex as a cartoon villain: try to understand whatever was true in their perspective too, including the conflicts they were carrying inside themselves.
Sometimes the easiest story is that they were fake all along, because it explains everything.
Grab it only if it really is the simplest explanation of what happened, and even the curiosity about that can be therapeutic for you.
People who aren’t heavily invested in seeing your innocence can help you tell, and a therapist, pastor, or even a stranger may see the evidence more clearly than a lifelong friend.
Spiritual practice during an ending is critical, but don’t use it to get around the feelings.
Pray for your ex’s wellbeing.
Remember what was real and good, and don’t use your pain as permission to hate them.
Avoid the New Age belief that everyone is simply a mirror of you.
Of course, we do partly mirror one another, but each person was formed by plenty that had nothing to do with you.
No matter how enlightened the Buddha was, his cousin Devadatta still kept trying to kill him: looking honestly at your part doesn’t erase theirs.
Sometimes it helps to ask, “What would Mr. Rogers do?” (if you’re old enough to remember that show).
I also learned that public demonization doesn’t always have to be the last chapter, even if things ended on that bitter note.
If you avoid contact forever, they might never apologize and learn honesty.
But it can help to keep distance for a while until cooler heads prevail.
On the other hand, it can be tempting to let them back into your life after a private apology, and especially after a public one, but keep in mind you deserve a stable love.
You’re not a yo-yo.
